portInfo.description: Vancouver’s Alaska homeport is the Canada Place cruise terminal on the downtown waterfront, owned and operated by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority. Canada Place states the terminal welcomes over one million passengers a year, describes a three-berth facility that can service up to four ships, and notes shore-power capability completed in 2009. Postal framing: Canada Place c/o VFPA, 100 The Pointe, 999 Canada Place, Vancouver, B.C. V6C 3T4. VFPA passenger FAQs: baggage check typically starts 10:00–10:30 a.m. Pacific on sailing day; passengers clear U.S. CBP pre-boarding inspection because ships are treated as U.S. jurisdiction for that step; disembarking passengers clear CBSA with declaration card E311. Door-threshold coordinates remain null.

gettingThere.distanceToCity: Transit. Waterfront Station via SkyTrain, SeaBus, West Coast Express. Parking. Underground parkade operated by Indigo Park Canada; entry at foot of Howe Street. YVR. Canada Line to Waterfront is the logical rail path; timed fare quotes Not verified on the Canada Place page captured. Bag drop. 10:00–10:30 a.m. Pacific sailing-day window per VFPA.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: On Alaska embarkation mornings, budget time for baggage drop + screening + U.S. CBP pre-inspection in sequence — VFPA lists CBP as the final step before boarding.
